knowledge:
- key_parameters: database=The first argument of path_enrich, specifying the pathway database to use ("KEGG", "REAC", or "WP") ;; meta=A vector of metabolite IDs, which must be KEGG compound IDs ;; genes=A vector of gene IDs, which must be gene symbols
- alternatives: The documentation mentions using gprofiler2 for gene pathway enrichment, MPINet for metabolite pathway enrichment, clusterProfiler for GO term enrichment, and PaxtoolsR/graphite for direct interaction extraction.
- when_to_use: Use when you have a list of gene symbols and KEGG compound IDs from a multi-omics study and want to perform integrated pathway enrichment, network interaction analysis, and interactive visualization.
- pitfalls: Metabolite IDs must be KEGG compound IDs and gene IDs must be gene symbols ;; The interactions function strictly requires results from path_enrich run on all three databases ("KEGG", "REAC", and "WP") ;; Some user elements may not be present in the enriched pathways and will be filtered out of the main visualization (though they are listed in a separate tab).

workflows.name: famat_analysis_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Perform integrated pathway enrichment, interaction network analysis, and GO enrichment on gene and metabolite lists, and visualize the results in a Shiny app.
workflows.stages: 1. Run pathway enrichment analysis for KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways using path_enrich ;; 2. Extract direct interactions and calculate centrality using interactions ;; 3. Complete the data with GO term enrichment and pathway filtering using compl_data ;; 4. Launch the interactive Shiny application using rshiny
workflows.code:
data(genes)
data(meta)
data(all_compounds_chebi)

listk <- path_enrich("KEGG", meta, genes)
listr <- path_enrich("REAC", meta, genes)
listw <- path_enrich("WP", meta, genes)

interactions_result <- interactions(listk, listr, listw)

compl_data_result <- compl_data(interactions_result)

rshiny(compl_data_result)
